verdict.rationale: Plausible's own docs state it collects no personal data and that you do not need cookie banners for analytics or consent for tracking. A first-party script proxy is also supported. Community posts back this up independently: one says no IP addresses are stored or used to build profiles, another describes unique visitors being counted with a daily-salted hash rather than cookies (with a noted VPN-counting caveat), and one raises a speculative IP concern that another commenter answers. missing for 10: explicit first-party technical documentation of the cookieless counting mechanism (the evidence shows outcomes such as 'no consent banner' rather than a detailed 'no cookies' spec).
